2.text: was ten years old. On the second day after her death he took his own life

3.text: by stabbing himself with a knife. “I want to follow her,” he said before

4.text: he died. Another case illustrating the strong attachment between husband

5.text: and wife is that of an old man living in the Dry Anui district, who had

6.text: lived with his wife for half a century. Suddenly he declared that he wanted to

7.text: take a certain girl of the vicinity for his second wife. His old wife threatened

8.text: to return to her own relatives if he should take the girl. The old couple had

9.text: no children living who might have prevented the dissolution of that marriage.

10.text: The old man hesitated for some time; but his desire to have children — if

11.text: not begotten by himself, then at least the issue of the customary group-

12.text: marriage — prevailed, and he took the young woman. His first wife kept

13.text: her word and left the camp, going to her brother, who lived at a distance

14.text: of a hundred miles. For a few months the old man lived with his young

15.text: wife; then he repined. He felt too proud, however, to go and see his old

16.text: mate. Rather than do that, he requested that he be killed, which was done

17.text: by strangulation with a rope.¹ Thus it will be seen that the married life of

18.text: the Chukchee is not exempt from strong feelings and romantic episodes.

19.text: POSITION OF CHILDREN. — I mentioned before that small children are an

20.text: object of great care and tenderness on the part of their parents. The endearing

21.text: term for children frequently used in common parlance is “little eggs” (lig̣liqqäiti).

22.text: The children are fed with the best morsels, and fondled and caressed by all

23.text: grown-up people. The tender love of parents for their children has found

24.text: expression in one episode which is repeated in many tales. A young boy

25.text: dies a sudden death. His parents, in great sorrow, remain in the sleeping-

26.text: room. The dead body is lying before them upon the ground on a reindeer-

27.text: skin. They weep day and night. Their cheeks are furrowed with tears to

28.text: the very bones. Thus they stay for one year, then for another, then for a

30.text: The childhood of Chukchee children is quite happy. They grow up free

31.text: and fearless in the freedom of camp life. Small boys are given knives just

32.text: as soon as they can grasp the handles, and from that time on they learn

33.text: gradually the use of this all-important implement. I have seen a small boy

34.text: try to carve wood with a knife hardly shorter than the boy himself. One

35.text: time a Cossack who accompanied me teased a boy about five years of age.

36.text: The little man took offence, took up a hatchet that was lying on the ground,

37.text: and flung it at the head of the man. His aim was accurate enough, though

38.text: the hatchet did not reach the amazed Cossack, who began to howl and stamp

39.text: his feet, intending to frighten the little warrior. Nothing daunted, the boy

40.text: caught up a big knife and turned upon his enemy.

41.text: The heroic tales of the Chukchee also make mention of young boys

42.text: taking part in combats and coming to the assistance of their parents. For
